title: What is known about 1RB0LD_0RC---_1LD0RF_0LE0RA_0RA1LF_0LA1LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_0RC---_1LD0RF_0LE0RA_0RA1LF_0LA1LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

The left end is a run of 011 after the head's cells (A>0 0 1 (011)^n), one copy longer at each visit to the left end (13 at step 1,530,193,864, 14 at step 1,815,265,479). The right end is a run of 10. In between lies an irregular word of 10, 110 and 1000. No exact rule has been found.
verdict: The question is open. The machine can halt only from A> 0 1 or 1 F> 1 (both directions proved in Lean); in 20,000,000,000 steps that never happens. In the first 109 steps A never had 0 1 under and after it (its contexts are 0 0 and 1 0), and F reading a 1 never had a 1 on its left (ctxcount M 1e9 F 2 -1: 0 0, 0 1, 1 0). No near misses at all.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 225 cells have been visited and 97 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.038). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.022).

claims.title: The halting context
claims.text: From A> 0 1 the machine reaches its halting transition (proved step by step, then step_none_iff). The halting transition is B reading a 1. B is entered from A reading a 0 (A writes 1 and moves right), or from F reading a 1 (F writes 1 and moves left), so the machine halts exactly from A> 0 1 or 1 F> 1 (Lean: halt_ctx, halt_ctx_F for the steps to the halt; halt_pred_1 for the converse, that every configuration halting one step later matches one of the two).

claims.title: Every halt passes through these two
claims.text: The converse of the halting context: every configuration that halts after exactly one more step is A> 0 1 or 1 F> 1 (halt_pred_1; both directions: halt_iff_1; after exactly two more steps: D> 1 0 1, E> 0 0 1 or 1 1 E> 1, halt_pred_2). So if the machine halts from blank tape, its run passes through one of the two (halts_blank_pred_1). The windows are found by a case split on the cells the head reads, and each case is evaluated with the library's step.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: 9 shift rules over the words of the tape (for example C> (110)^n becomes (010)^n C> in 7n steps and 0 F> (1)^n becomes (0)^n 0 F> in 3n steps), proved for every n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 20,000,000,000 steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c runs 20,000,000,000 steps without a halt; the visited tape is 247 cells wide and holds 107 ones.

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: In the first 109 steps A never had 0 1 under and after it (its contexts are 0 0 and 1 0), and F reading a 1 never had a 1 on its left (ctxcount M 1e9 F 2 -1: 0 0, 0 1, 1 0). No near misses at all.

claims.title: Growth
claims.text: Both ends grow logarithmically; the visits to the left end come at exponentially spaced times.

claims.title: Two local laws
claims.text: In 109 steps the cell right of A is always 0 (225,806,362 times: A> 0 0 161,290,275, A> 1 0 64,516,087) and F reading a 1 never has a 1 on its left (contexts 0 F> 0, 0 F> 1, 1 F> 0 only). The halt needs one of the two broken: A> 0 1 or 1 F> 1.

claims.title: Runs on the tape
claims.text: In 300 tapes sampled every 1,000,003 steps up to 3·108, the runs of 1s strictly inside the tape have length 1 or 2 (18,353 and 3,584 runs) and the runs of 0s length 1 to 6 (15,031, 1,983, 5,181, 21, 16, 4). Three 1s in a row do occur (first at step 5,506 at the left end of the tape, 1 0 1^3 B>0 ...; after step 107 first at step 170,930,892).

claims.title: No small finite-automata certificate
claims.text: A finite-automata-reduction search (a DFA of n states on one side of the head, the least co-closed NFA on (state × DFA state) + bottom for the other) finds no certificate with n ≤ 7 (23,836,540 DFAs at n = 7), with the DFA on the left or on the right.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Neither halting context has ever been approached, which points to a local invariant (A is entered after a write of 0 to its left or right, and the words of the tape keep a 0 after every place A starts on a 0); it is not proved. A windowed closed tape language (bbtools.ctl) with windows up to 7 cells does not exclude the halt.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine has run 20,000,000,000 steps without stopping. Its tape is a slow counter with a run of 011 on the left and a run of 10 on the right. It can stop only from two local patterns, A> 0 1 and 1 F> 1, neither of which it has ever produced.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 247 cells visited.
The only two contexts one step before the halt: both halt, and nothing else does (Lean: halt_ctx, halt_ctx_F, halt_pred_1).
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.038). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.022).
After 109 steps the tape spans 225 cells (168 left of the start, 50 right), with a density of 1s of 0.431.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: What the tape looks like
html: The left end is a run of 011 after the head's cells (A>0 0 1 (011)^n), one copy longer at each visit to the left end (13 at step 1,530,193,864, 14 at step 1,815,265,479). The right end is a run of 10. In between lies an irregular word of 10, 110 and 1000. No exact rule has been found.

sections.heading: The two ways to stop
html: The halting transition is B reading a 1. B is entered from A reading a 0 (A writes 1 and moves right), or from F reading a 1 (F writes 1 and moves left), so the machine halts exactly from A> 0 1 or 1 F> 1 (Lean: halt_ctx, halt_ctx_F for the steps to the halt; halt_pred_1 for the converse, that every configuration halting one step later matches one of the two). So the machine halts exactly when it produces A> 0 1 or 1 F> 1.
How close does it come? What A has ahead of it, counted at every step of the first 109 steps:

In the first 109 steps A never had 0 1 under and after it (its contexts are 0 0 and 1 0), and F reading a 1 never had a 1 on its left (ctxcount M 1e9 F 2 -1: 0 0, 0 1, 1 0). No near misses at all.

sections.heading: What a proof would need
html: Not known. Neither halting context has ever been approached, which points to a local invariant (A is entered after a write of 0 to its left or right, and the words of the tape keep a 0 after every place A starts on a 0); it is not proved. A windowed closed tape language (bbtools.ctl) with windows up to 7 cells does not exclude the halt.

The basic moves are proved in Lean for every length (lean/Rules.lean: crossing a run of one word in a fixed number of steps per copy), so a proof would need only the rule of the counter on top of them.

sections.heading: Two cells that are always 0
html: The machine stops when B reads a 1. B is entered from A on a 0 (A writes 1 and moves right) and from F on a 1 (F moves left), so it halts exactly when A, on a 0, has a 1 to its right, or when F, on a 1, has a 1 to its left. In the first 109 steps neither ever happens:

headwhat is next to ittimes
A> 0 00 on the right161,290,275
A> 1 00 on the right64,516,087
A> x 1a 1 on the right0
1 F> 1a 1 on the left0

These look like local facts, but no small automaton proves them: the reason lies in how the words 10, 110 and 1000 of the middle of the tape are laid out, which the automata tried (windows of up to 8 cells, finite automata reduction with up to 7 states) do not capture.

summary: A run of 011 on the left, of 10 on the right and an irregular word between; halts only from A> 01 or 1 F> 1, neither ever approached in 2·10^10 steps.
